```{julia}
using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end
```

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

"""
    ereturn_list(m)

Stata-style `ereturn list` for a regression object `m` (FixedEffectModels /
GLM / StatsBase-compatible). Prints scalars, macros, and matrices, and
returns them in a NamedTuple so they can be retrieved programmatically.
"""
function ereturn_list(m)
    _try(f, m) = try f(m) catch; missing end

    scalars = (;
        N          = _try(StatsBase.nobs, m),
        df_m       = _try(StatsBase.dof, m),
        df_r       = _try(StatsBase.dof_residual, m),
        r2         = _try(StatsBase.r2, m),
        r2_a       = _try(StatsBase.adjr2, m),
        rss        = _try(StatsBase.deviance, m),
        rmse       = (rss = _try(StatsBase.deviance, m); dfr = _try(StatsBase.dof_residual, m);
                      (ismissing(rss) || ismissing(dfr) || dfr == 0) ? missing : sqrt(rss / dfr)),
        F          = hasproperty(m, :F) ? m.F : missing,
        p          = hasproperty(m, :p) ? m.p : missing,
    )
    macros = (;
        depvar  = hasproperty(m, :yname)   ? string(m.yname)   : missing,
        indeps  = try join(string.(StatsBase.coefnames(m)), " ") catch; missing end,
        cmd     = string(nameof(typeof(m))),
    )
    b = _try(StatsBase.coef, m)
    V = _try(StatsBase.vcov, m)

    println("scalars:")
    for (k, v) in pairs(scalars)
        ismissing(v) && continue
        println("  e($k) = ", v isa Real ? round(v; sigdigits=8) : v)
    end
    println("\nmacros:")
    for (k, v) in pairs(macros)
        ismissing(v) && continue
        println("  e($k) : \"", v, "\"")
    end
    println("\nmatrices:")
    if !ismissing(b)
        names_ = try StatsBase.coefnames(m) catch; ["x$i" for i in eachindex(b)] end
        println("  e(b)  : 1 x $(length(b))")
        _pt_compat(reshape(b, 1, :); header = names_)
    end
    if !ismissing(V)
        println("  e(V)  : $(size(V,1)) x $(size(V,2))")
        names_ = try StatsBase.coefnames(m) catch; ["x$i" for i in 1:size(V,1)] end
        _pt_compat(V; header = names_, row_labels = names_)
    end
    return (; scalars, macros, b, V)
end
```

```{julia}
#=
* Factor variables for interaction between categorical and continuous variables
summarize i.rep78#c.weight
=#
#=
* Factor variables for interaction between categorical and continuous variables
summarize i.rep78#c.weight
=#
# summarize i.rep78#i.foreign, allbaselevels
# Drop rows where either factor is missing, then build a 0/1 dummy for every (rep78, foreign) cell
sub   = dropmissing(auto[:, [:rep78, :foreign]])
rep78v  = [_rawval(v) for v in sub.rep78]
foreignv = [_rawval(v) for v in sub.foreign]
rlevs = sort(unique(rep78v))
flevs = sort(unique(foreignv))
dummies = DataFrame((Symbol("$(Int(r)).rep78#$(Int(f)).foreign") =>
                     Int.((rep78v .== r) .& (foreignv .== f))
                     for r in rlevs, f in flevs)...)
summarize_stata(dummies)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Factor variables for interaction between two continuous variables
regress mpg price c.weight c.weight#c.weight, noheader
=#
#=
* Factor variables for interaction between two continuous variables
regress mpg price c.weight c.weight#c.weight, noheader
=#
# summarize i.rep78#c.weight
# For each level r of rep78: weight when rep78==r, else 0 (drop rows where rep78 is missing)
sub = dropmissing(auto[:, [:rep78, :weight]])
rep78v = [_rawval(v) for v in sub.rep78]
wv     = Float64.(sub.weight)
rlevs  = sort(unique(rep78v))
inter = DataFrame((Symbol("$(Int(r)).rep78#c.weight") =>
                   ifelse.(rep78v .== r, wv, 0.0) for r in rlevs)...)
summarize_stata(inter)
```

```{julia}
# Factor variables for interaction between two continuous variables
# regress mpg price c.weight c.weight#c.weight
# NOTE: auto.dta stores weight as Int16 — squaring Int16 overflows silently in Julia,
# so we cast to Float64 first to match Stata's numeric precision.
auto.weight_sq = Float64.(auto.weight) .^ 2
model_sq = FixedEffectModels.reg(auto, @formula(mpg ~ price + weight + weight_sq))
println(model_sq)
```

### 1.4.4 A three-step process

1. Create or change the do-file.
2. Execute the do-file in Stata.
3. Read the resulting log with a text editor.

### 1.4.5 Comments and long lines

```{julia}
#=
* Demonstrate use of comments
* This program reads in system file auto.dta and gets summary statistics
clear // Remove data from memory
* The next code shows how to allow a single command to span two lines
sysuse ///
auto.dta
```

## 1.6 Using results from Stata commands

### 1.6.1 Using results from the r-class command summarize

```{julia}
#=
* Illustrate use of return list for r-class command summarize
summarize mpg
=#
#=
* Illustrate use of return list for r-class command summarize
summarize mpg
=#
# Illustrate use of summary statistics for mpg
println("Summary of mpg:")
println("  N     = ", length(auto.mpg))
println("  Mean  = ", round(mean(auto.mpg), digits=4))
println("  Std   = ", round(std(auto.mpg), digits=4))
println("  Min   = ", minimum(auto.mpg))
println("  Max   = ", maximum(auto.mpg))
```

```{julia}
#=
return list
=#
#=
return list
=#
summarize_stata(auto, :mpg)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Illustrate use of r()
quietly summarize mpg
scalar range = r(max) - r(min)
display "Sample range = " range
=#
#=
* Illustrate use of r()
quietly summarize mpg
scalar range = r(max) - r(min)
display "Sample range = " range
=#
# return list equivalent - stored results
r_mean = mean(auto.mpg)
r_sd   = std(auto.mpg)
r_min  = minimum(auto.mpg)
r_max  = maximum(auto.mpg)
r_N    = length(auto.mpg)
r_sum  = sum(auto.mpg)
println("r(N)    = ", r_N)
println("r(mean) = ", r_mean)
println("r(Var) = ", r_sd^2)
println("r(sd)   = ", r_sd)
println("r(min)  = ", r_min)
println("r(max)  = ", r_max)
println("r(sum)  = ", r_sum)
```

### 1.6.2 Using results from the e-class command regress

```{julia}

println(model_ols)
```

```{julia}

* *ereturn list after e-class command regress

```

```{julia}
#=
* Use of e() where scalar
scalar r2 = e(mss ) / ( e(mss) + e(rss) )
display "r-squared = " r2
=#
#=
* Use of e() where scalar
scalar r2 = e(mss ) / ( e(mss) + e(rss) )
display "r-squared = " r2
=#
# ereturn list after regress
println("Number of obs = ", StatsBase.nobs(model_ols))
println("R-squared     = ", round(StatsBase.r2(model_ols), digits=6))
println("Adj R-squared = ", round(StatsBase.adjr2(model_ols), digits=6))
println("Coefficients  = ", StatsBase.coef(model_ols))
println("Std errors    = ", StatsBase.stderror(model_ols))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Use of e() where matrix
matrix best = e(b)
scalar bprice = best[1,1]
matrix Vest = e(V)
scalar Vprice = Vest[1,1]
scalar tprice = bprice/sqrt(Vprice)
display "t statistic for H O : b_price = 0 is " tprice
=#
#=
* Use of e() where matrix
matrix best = e(b)
scalar bprice = best[1,1]
matrix Vest = e(V)
scalar Vprice = Vest[1,1]
scalar tprice = bprice/sqrt(Vprice)
display "t statistic for H O : b_price = 0 is " tprice
=#
# Use of e() where scalar -- compute R-squared manually
tss = sum((auto.mpg .- mean(auto.mpg)).^2)
rss = GLM.deviance(model_ols)
r2_manual = 1 - rss / tss
println("r-squared = ", round(r2_manual, digits=6))
```

```{julia}
# Use of e() where matrix
best   = StatsBase.coef(model_ols)
bprice = best[2]  # coefficient on price
Vest   = StatsBase.vcov(model_ols)
Vprice = Vest[2, 2]
tprice = bprice / sqrt(Vprice)
println("t statistic for H0: b_price = 0 is ", round(tprice, digits=4))
```

## 1.7 Global and local macros

### 1.7.1 Global macros

```{julia}
#=
* Global macro definition and use
global xlist price weight
regress mpg $xlist , noheader // $ prefix is necessary
=#
#=
* Global macro definition and use
global xlist price weight
regress mpg $xlist , noheader // $ prefix is necessary
=#
# Global macro definition and use
xlist = [:price, :weight]
f = Term(:mpg) ~ sum(Term.(xlist))
model_g = FixedEffectModels.reg(auto, f)
println(model_g)
```

### 1.7.2 local macros

```{julia}
#=
* Local macro definition and use
local xlist "price weigh"
regress mpg `xlist', noheader // single quotes are necessary
=#
#=
* Local macro definition and use
local xlist "price weigh"
regress mpg `xlist', noheader // single quotes are necessary
=#
# Local macro definition and use
xlist = [:price, :weight]
f = Term(:mpg) ~ sum(Term.(xlist))
model_l = FixedEffectModels.reg(auto, f)
println(model_l)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Local macro definition without double quotes
local y mpg
regress `y' `xlist', noheader
=#
#=
* Local macro definition without double quotes
local y mpg
regress `y' `xlist', noheader
=#
# Local macro definition without double quotes
y = :mpg
f = Term(y) ~ sum(Term.(xlist))
model_l2 = FixedEffectModels.reg(auto, f)
println(model_l2)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Local macro definition through function evaluation
local z = 2+2
display `z'
=#
#=
* Local macro definition through function evaluation
local z = 2+2
display `z'
=#
# Local macro definition through function evaluation
z = 2 + 2
println(z)
```

### 1.7.3 Scalar or macro?

```{julia}
#=
* Scalars disappear after clear all but macro does not
global b 3
local c 4
scalar d = 5
clear
display $b_ _skip(3) `c' // display macros
=#
#=
* Scalars disappear after clear all but macro does not
global b 3
local c 4
scalar d = 5
clear
display $b_ _skip(3) `c' // display macros
=#
# In Julia, variables persist until they go out of scope
b = 3
c = 4
d = 5
println(b, "   ", c)  # display variables
```

```{julia}
#=
* display the scalar
display d 
=#
#=
* display the scalar
display d 
=#
# display the scalar
println(d)
```

```{julia}
#=
clear all
display $b _skip(3) `c' // display macros
=#
#=
clear all
display $b _skip(3) `c' // display macros
=#
# After clearing workspace, variables are gone
# In Julia, variables remain in scope unless explicitly removed
println(b, "   ", c)
```

## 1.8 Looping commands

```{julia}
#=
* Make artificial dataset of 100 observations on 4 uniform variables
clear
set obs 100
*obs was 0 , now 100
set seed 10101
generate x1var = runiform()
generate x2var = runiform()
generate x3var = runiform()
generate x4var = runiform()
=#
#=
* Make artificial dataset of 100 observations on 4 uniform variables
clear
set obs 100
*obs was 0 , now 100
set seed 10101
generate x1var = runiform()
generate x2var = runiform()
generate x3var = runiform()
generate x4var = runiform()
=#
# Make artificial dataset of 100 observations on 4 uniform variables
Random.seed!(10101)
df_loop = DataFrame(
    x1var = Random.rand(100),
    x2var = Random.rand(100),
    x3var = Random.rand(100),
    x4var = Random.rand(100)
)
```

```{julia}
#=
* Manually obtain the sum of four variables
generate sum = x1var + x2var + x3var + x4var
summarize sum
=#
#=
* Manually obtain the sum of four variables
generate sum = x1var + x2var + x3var + x4var
summarize sum
=#
# Manually obtain the sum of four variables
df_loop.sum_var = df_loop.x1var .+ df_loop.x2var .+ df_loop.x3var .+ df_loop.x4var
println("Summary of sum:")
println("  N    = ", length(df_loop.sum_var))
println("  Mean = ", round(mean(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
println("  Std  = ", round(std(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
println("  Min  = ", round(minimum(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
println("  Max  = ", round(maximum(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
```

### 1.8.1 The foreach loop

```{julia}
#=
* foreach loop with a variable list
quietly replace sum = 0
foreach var of varlist x1var x2var x3var x4var {
    quietly replace sum = sum + `var'
    }
summarize sum
=#
#=
* foreach loop with a variable list
quietly replace sum = 0
foreach var of varlist x1var x2var x3var x4var {
    quietly replace sum = sum + `var'
    }
summarize sum
=#
# foreach loop with a variable list
df_loop.sum_var .= 0.0
for var in [:x1var, :x2var, :x3var, :x4var]
    df_loop.sum_var .+= df_loop[!, var]
end
println("Summary of sum (foreach):")
println("  Mean = ", round(mean(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
println("  Std  = ", round(std(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
```

### 1.8.2 The forvalues loop

```{julia}
#=
* forvalues loop to create a swn of variables
quietly replace sum = 0
forvalues i = 1/4 {
    quietly replace sum = sum + x`i'var
    }
summarize sum
=#
#=
* forvalues loop to create a swn of variables
quietly replace sum = 0
forvalues i = 1/4 {
    quietly replace sum = sum + x`i'var
    }
summarize sum
=#
# forvalues loop to create a sum of variables
df_loop.sum_var .= 0.0
for i in 1:4
    df_loop.sum_var .+= df_loop[!, Symbol("x$(i)var")]
end
println("Summary of sum (forvalues):")
println("  Mean = ", round(mean(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
println("  Std  = ", round(std(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
```

```{julia}
#=

* foreach loop with a number list

}

=#
#=
// Not included in book
* foreach loop with a number list
quietly replace sum = 0
foreach i of numlist 1 2 3 4 {
    quietly replace sum = sum + x`i'var
}
summarize sum
=#
# foreach loop with a number list
df_loop.sum_var .= 0.0
for i in [1, 2, 3, 4]
    df_loop.sum_var .+= df_loop[!, Symbol("x$(i)var")]
end
println("Summary of sum (numlist):")

```

### 1.8.3 The while loop

```{julia}
#=
* While loop and local macros to create a sum of variables
quietly replace sum = 0
local i 1
while `i' <= 4 {
    quietly replace sum = sum + x`i'var
    local i = `i' + 1
    }
summarize sum
=#
#=
* While loop and local macros to create a sum of variables
quietly replace sum = 0
local i 1
while `i' <= 4 {
    quietly replace sum = sum + x`i'var
    local i = `i' + 1
    }
summarize sum
=#
# While loop and local variables to create a sum of variables
df_loop.sum_var .= 0.0
i = 1
while i <= 4
    df_loop.sum_var .+= df_loop[!, Symbol("x$(i)var")]
    i += 1
end
println("Summary of sum (while):")
println("  Mean = ", round(mean(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
println("  Std  = ", round(std(df_loop.sum_var), digits=4))
```

## 1.10 Template do-file

```{julia}
#=
*log close
* 1. Program name
* mus01p2template.do is a template do-file
* 2. Write output to a log file
log using musr/mus01p2template.txt, text replace
* 3. Stata version
version 10.1 // so will still run in a later version o f Stata
* 4. Program explanation
*This illustrative program creates 100 uniform variates
* 5. Change Stata default settings - two examples are given
set more off // scroll screen output by at full speed
set mem 20m // set aside 20 mb for memory space
* 6. Set program parameters using global macros
global numobs 100
local seed 10101
local xlist xvar
* 7. Generate data and summarize
set obs $numobs
set seed `seed'
generate xvar = runiform()
generate yvar = xvar^2
summarize
* 8. Demonstrate use of results stored in r ()
summarize xvar
display "Sample range = " r(max)-r(min)
regress yvar `xlist'
scalar r2 = e(mss) / ( e(mss)+e(rss) )
display "r-squared = " r2
* 9. Close output file and exit Stata
log close
exit, clear
=#
#=
*log close
* 1. Program name
* mus01p2template.do is a template do-file
* 2. Write output to a log file
log using musr/mus01p2template.txt, text replace
* 3. Stata version
version 10.1 // so will still run in a later version o f Stata
* 4. Program explanation
*This illustrative program creates 100 uniform variates
* 5. Change Stata default settings - two examples are given
set more off // scroll screen output by at full speed
set mem 20m // set aside 20 mb for memory space
* 6. Set program parameters using global macros
global numobs 100
local seed 10101
local xlist xvar
* 7. Generate data and summarize
set obs $numobs
set seed `seed'
generate xvar = runiform()
generate yvar = xvar^2
summarize
* 8. Demonstrate use of results stored in r ()
summarize xvar
display "Sample range = " r(max)-r(min)
regress yvar `xlist'
scalar r2 = e(mss) / ( e(mss)+e(rss) )
display "r-squared = " r2
* 9. Close output file and exit Stata
log close
exit, clear
=#
# mus01p2template.jl is a template script
# Julia equivalent of Stata template do-file

# Program parameters
numobs = 100
seed   = 10101

# Generate data and summarize
Random.seed!(seed)
df_template = DataFrame(xvar = Random.rand(numobs))
df_template.yvar = df_template.xvar .^ 2
println("Summary:")
println(DataFrames.describe(df_template))

# Demonstrate use of stored results
xmean = mean(df_template.xvar)
xmin  = minimum(df_template.xvar)
xmax  = maximum(df_template.xvar)
println("\nSample range = ", xmax - xmin)

# Regression
model_template = FixedEffectModels.reg(df_template, @formula(yvar ~ xvar))
r2_val = StatsBase.r2(model_template)
println("r-squared = ", round(r2_val, digits=6))
```
